pr_title: Apply Precision/Scale/Offset to struct in modbus sensor
pr_body:
The single values in struct are corrected with presicion, scale and offset,
just as it is done with single values.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
the struct configuration e.g.
```yaml
sensors:
  - name test1
  - data_type = custom
  - count = 8
  - struct = ">4f"
```
Could result in very long strings being delivered back, due to many decimal digits.
```yaml
sensors:
  - name test1
  - data_type: custom
  - scale: 1
  - offset: 0
  - precision: 2
  - count: 8
  - struct: ">4f"
```
will cut the decimals to 2.

The modbus request is good, but I can't get my 4 sensors - 32 bits floats (16 bit inverted).

- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 5.4.83
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Supervised (VM QNAP)
- Integration causing this issue: Modbus
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13821602/102382666-fa498d00-3fca-11eb-9264-bbc9162013e0.png)

The reverse_order boolean option reverse the order of all registers, but the reversal of the order should be done for two consecutive 16-bit registers (for 32 bits float).
Unfortunately the byte order might differ between manufacturers of Modbus instruments.

Ideally, there should be varables configuration : byte and word swap. 
As described [https://store.chipkin.com/articles/how-real-floating-point-and-32-bit-data-is-encoded-in-modbus-rtu-messages](url)

Wouldn't we have a possibility to have an integer float... table (according to data_type) and to be able to access it with an index?

> Wouldn't we have a possibility to have an integer float... table

I'm not sure what you mean. We already have such a table but it's only for common data types. Floats are among them.

From `modbus/const.py`
```python
DEFAULT_STRUCT_FORMAT = {
    DATA_TYPE_INT: {1: "h", 2: "i", 4: "q"},
    DATA_TYPE_UINT: {1: "H", 2: "I", 4: "Q"},
    DATA_TYPE_FLOAT: {1: "e", 2: "f", 4: "d"},
}
```

Unless I'm mistaken, the existing table doesn't seem to be usable in the case of a multiple value reading.

I would like to be able to access all the values of a multiple float reading by indexing a table and not by parsing the floats separated by commas.
Doesn't the comma separator limit the number of Modbus variables read? (especially in the case of floats with many characters).

> ...the existing table doesn't seem to be usable in the case of a multiple value reading.

Yes, you're correct. This table is used to simplify reading of common types (read always as a single value). If lookup fails, the integration throws an error telling you to try custom schema.

> Doesn't the comma separator limit the number of Modbus variables read?

No (at least I am not aware of it). Basically, by defining the schema you tell Python how to parse incoming bits. Python returns an array of parsed values. The way of separating the values with comma is just the way how we represent this array in the UI.
